questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Choosing a destination where english was the main language spoken. Plus good options to travel and exploring while studying.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. UniMelb has a pretty good step by step guide to prepare you and their website is quite straight forward/easy to navigate. The only thing I struggled a bit with was figuring out their time tabling system regarding classes.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 is really good to help you with anything university related. They can be a bit slow to answer e-mails, but you can also just show up upon arrival and someone will be able to help you with whatever you need.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied to student accommodation through UniMelb and stayed at 'The Lofts', which was quite nice as only postgraduate students can live there, which means people are bit closer in age to danish students. However, it is first comes first serve so maybe look into it as soon as possible as the cheapest options sell out pretty fast. However, I also know other private operators such as Scape and Yugo provide student housing. Alternatively, 'fairy floss' on Facebook is suposed be the place to go for private accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is definitely expensive to live in student accommodation. But finding housing in Melbourne can be quite tricky and there are scammers out there. The general level of rent is also quite high, so I was quite satisfied with paying a bit extra and then have everything go a bit more smooth.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As mentioned above, it is quit straight forward. However, I did have a bit technical problems with registrering for BA classes while being a KA student. But if you just reach out to Stop 1, they will help with everything.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Just follow their step by step guide and everything should be good

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop 1

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, I did have a few technical issues but Stop 1 helped to sort it out. However, when applying for tutorial times don't get surprised it you don't get allocated to the the ones you wished for. All my tutorial timeslots ended up being changed anyways, and you can always change around - even after the semester has started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the handbook when navigating subjects, and maybe try and avoid subjects with mandatory attendance. At least I found that a bit annoying.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was way below University of Copenhagen, both at BA and MA. I discovered that a lot of the business and economics related subjects had a very high percentage of students from Asia, who didn't really speak english that well. Unfortunately, this really affected the level of teaching as class discussions or group work was either impossible or very awkward.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same with a mix of lectures and tutorials. However, the exam style was quite different as you had to turn in assignments all throughout the semester which would then make up your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Public Relations and Communications, Politics and the Media, Campaigns and Elections + Public Policy Lobbying Strategies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Public Policy Lobbying Strategies was a really interesting as it was a bit more hands on compared to courses at UCPH and the teaching staff were just amazing.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When moving in to 'The Lofts' the apartment was almost completely empty so we had to buy bedding and kitchen stuff. You could also buy a package in advance but it was a bit expensive (2000 DKK) and much cheaper to just go to Kmart upon arrival.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was a bit cheaper to dine out compared to Copenhagen. However, in the grocery stores fruits and vegetables were quite expensive as well as dairy products such as cheese and yoghurt. I great tip saving tip is using 'Union Mart' on campus where you can access free groceries, and they also host events multiple times a week with free food/meals on campus. You can check out their instagram on @umsu_welfare.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of clubs at uni, and you can meet them all during O-week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally didn't join any, but did go to the pub crawl hosted by the surf club which I highly recommend, it was so much fun. It definitely seemed like a very social club with lots of parties if you're into that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is so much do, but some of my personal highlight were Tasmania and Great Ocean Road + Grampians. But remember to get an international drivers license so you can go on roadtrips!!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, Melbourne feels quite European

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Honestly, I didn't really make any local friends. But maybe through some of the clubs???

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: All the coffee shops close really early, like 2 or 3 pm. Maybe not the biggest thing, but I did find it quite annoying.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aussies are quite outgoing

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just do it!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience living in another country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the time and planning that goes into it beforehand. But it is all worth it in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
